prerequisites: A competence in English corresponding at least to B1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFRL)

learning_outcomes.text: Train students of Engineering to reach a language competence in English corresponding to level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), in relation to the four basic language skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing), with special emphasis on some genres of specialised and professional communication, such as project descriptions, project proposals for design competitions and reports.
Understanding globally and selectively both oral and written texts on topics belonging to the personal and social sphere and to English for Biomedical, and Electronic Engineering.

Taking part in conversations and interact in discussions in a way appropriate to the context in different social and professional communicative situations; being able to write simple texts of personal and professional content.

Producing linear and cohesive oral and written texts to refer facts and describe situations connected to personal experiences and to the specialised field of Biomedical and Electronic Engineering; analysing, rephrasing and summarising simple texts on professional topics.

Ability to select, analyze, apply critically one’s own judgment to the materials, the situations and the areas of study and work; reflecting on the linguistic system (phonology, morphology, syntax, lexicon) and on language uses (functions, variety of registers and texts, etc.), also in a comparative perspective, in order to identify analogies and differences with the Italian language.

Acquiring skills and competences useful to obtain success in the world of work and in society (life skills e soft skills); reinforcing foreign language learning strategies in order to develop study autonomy; enhancing professional lexis and topics in the English language, by using texts and materials drawn from various sources.

syllabus_topics: English for Special Purposes (ESP), namely technical language for Biomedical and Electronic Engineering
Grammar and syntax of B2 CEFRL levels: nouns and articles
Expressing habits: “be used to”, “used to”, “get used to”
Formal and written English vs spoken English
Communicative functions of B2 CEFR Levels: talking about oneself and other people
Describing actions (habits and ongoing actions), places, people and professions
Writing an email and an accurate CV
Taking part effectively in job interviews
Topics and specific lexis: Italian, British and American education systems
A university in an English speaking country
Phonetic transcription and pronunciation in keeping with the International Phonetic Alphabet
Main varieties of English: British and American Englishes
Specific lexicon related to Biomedical and Electronic Engineering within the topics dealt with during the course
Presentation of a student’s work connected to a professional area
teaching_methods: Active participation through guided tasks and oral presentations
Exam simulations on the e-learning platform UNISANNIO Handy
assessment_rules: The final exam consists of a written test and an oral interview, each making up 50% of the final mark. To pass the written test, a mark of at least 18/30 is required, which is a precondition to access the oral test. The written test includes a grammar section and a short composition or a listening comprehension activity. The oral test covers personal and professional topics, course topics, presentation of a professional topic, and discussion of the written test.
